sections.html:
Everett is the Snohomish County seat. A sale here runs through county offices for excise tax and property tax, and through the city for any permit questions. Population is 113,567, up from 110,629 at the 2020 census.

Only 49.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so a good share of sellers are landlords, heirs who inherited a rental, or owners of a house with a basement or backyard unit. That mix decides which sale route fits. A vacant inherited house, a tenant-occupied duplex and a move-in-ready home on Rucker Hill each call for a different plan.

Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $565,300. That number covers the whole city, not your house. Condition, lot and street all move the price, so use it as a rough backdrop only.

Everett has 19 recognized neighborhood associations, and buyers shop by area. A few come up often:

  • Bayside and Port Gardner: downtown, the waterfront and the historic Rucker Hill residential area.
  • Northwest Everett and Riverside: older homes near Everett Community College, with historic districts in both.
  • Lowell: southeast of downtown and once its own town.
  • Silver Lake, Cascade View and Twin Creeks: south Everett, near Everett Mall and the lake.
  • Westmont: a mostly multifamily area in the southwest.

Most of the city is in Everett Public Schools. The southern and western neighborhoods are in the Mukilteo School District, so confirm the district for the address before you describe schools in a listing.

The southwestern neighborhoods include creek ravines that drain to Port Gardner Bay, and the area is prone to mudslides. If your lot sits on a slope or near a ravine, pull together drainage and retaining wall records before buyers ask for them.

sections.h2: Can I sell an Everett house that has an accessory dwelling unit?
sections.html:
Yes, and the city has loosened its rules. Accessory dwelling units are allowed in every zone except Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial. An ADU is a unit under 1,000 square feet that stays subordinate to the main home, and a lot can have up to two. Dwellings under 1,200 square feet need no off-street car parking.

Fees matter to the next owner. Transportation impact fees are waived for one added ADU, school impact fees are waived for ADUs, and park impact fees are cut by half. In June 2026 the city also launched a gallery of pre-approved ADU designs, with a licensing fee of about $1,500.

  • If the unit was built without a permit, ask Everett Permit Services at PermitServices@everettwa.gov what it takes to legalize it before you list.
  • Basements and attics count as ADU space, garages do not, and each separate dwelling unit needs its own utilities.
  • In a historic overlay, any ADU that is not entirely inside the existing home goes to the Historical Commission.

sections.h2: Your choices if you need to sell fast
sections.html:
Everett sellers usually pick among three routes. The right one depends on the house and the deadline.

  • List with an agent: the widest buyer pool, with showings, inspections and financing contingencies that add weeks.
  • Sell directly to an investor or cash buyer: fewer contingencies and a closing date you can often choose, usually at a price below a fully prepared listing.
  • Sell it yourself: you save a listing commission but handle the disclosure forms, pricing and negotiation.

Whichever route you take, ask for proof of funds and read the purchase agreement before signing. Then compare each offer to what you would net after taxes, liens and any loan payoff. A written estimate from the escrow company's closing officer shows those figures line by line.

Washington charges a real estate excise tax on each sale, and the seller usually pays it. The state portion is graduated under RCW 82.45.060: 1.1 percent of the first $525,000 of the price, 1.28 percent on the portion up to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent up to $3,025,000 and 3 percent above that. For sales beginning January 1, 2027 the first tier ends at $551,000. A local rate is added on top, so get the combined figure from the Snohomish County Treasurer or your escrow officer.

For a deeded transfer, the excise tax affidavit, the conveyance document and payment go to the county treasurer. The excise tax counter is open Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., at 3000 Rockefeller, Everett, WA 98201.

Property tax is billed in two halves, due April 30 and October 31. Mailed payments must be postmarked by the due date. If a second-half bill is still open when you sell, it carries interest and has to be cleared at closing. The first-half deadline after that is April 30, 2027.

Late payments carry interest. Under RCW 84.56.020, residential property with four or fewer units is charged 9 percent a year on delinquent taxes, with no added penalties. Larger or nonresidential property faces 12 percent plus penalties. The county assesses the charge on the first day of each month, and missing the April 30 first-half payment makes the full year's tax delinquent.

A property can go to foreclosure once the third delinquent year's taxes are owed in full. The county runs its Tax Lien Foreclosure Sale online, with the list of properties filed in court each May. If you are close to that point, a sale can pay the back taxes out of the proceeds at closing. A statute also allows interest and penalties to be waived in limited situations, so ask the Treasurer's office whether you qualify.

A sale moves faster when your paperwork is ready before the first offer arrives. Here is the usual order.

  • Get each offer in writing, with the price, the closing date and every cost assigned to you.
  • Ask the buyer for proof of funds and find out whether the offer depends on an inspection or financing.
  • Order a payoff statement from your lender so the loan balance is exact.
  • Gather permit records for any basement, backyard unit or addition, plus drainage records if your lot is on a slope.
  • Have escrow total the excise tax, any unpaid property tax and other closing costs so you can see your net.
  • Sign the deed and the excise tax affidavit, and make sure the payment reaches the county treasurer.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and loan approval, so the date is set mostly by title work and by when you want to hand over the keys. A listing sale adds showings, inspection negotiations and the buyer's financing timeline.

faqs.q: How many people live in Everett, WA?
faqs.a: Population is 113,567 as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 110,629. Everett is the most populous city in Snohomish County.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax when an Everett house sells?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays. If the seller does not, the buyer becomes responsible, and unpaid tax can become a lien on the property. The state tiers are in RCW 82.45.060, and a local rate is added.

faqs.q: Are accessory dwelling units allowed in Everett?
faqs.a: Yes. ADUs are allowed in every zone except Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial, with up to two per lot and a size cap of 1,000 square feet. Check the permit history of any existing unit before you sell.

faqs.q: When are Snohomish County property taxes due?
faqs.a: First-half or full payment is due April 30, and the second half is due October 31. Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Everett house?
faqs.a: Most of Everett is in Everett Public Schools, while the southern and western neighborhoods are served by the Mukilteo School District. Confirm the district for your exact address before you advertise schools.
